headline: Van Veen holds off Schindler surge to win 10-7
standfirst: Gian van Veen led 9-3 and needed an 11-dart break to stop Martin Schindler’s four-leg run, reaching the Grand Slam quarter-finals to face Nathan Aspinall.
body: Gian van Veen reached the quarter-finals of the Grand Slam of Darts with a 10-7 win over Martin Schindler, but a match that looked finished at 9-3 ended with the world No 3 needing his best leg of the night to close it.

Schindler won four in a row, the last a 10-dart break, to pull back to 9-7. Van Veen broke back at once in 11 darts, checking out 93 to win it. “You feel like you’re down because you’ve lost the last four or five legs,” he said afterwards.
Until then he had been in control. He broke throw five times in all and averaged 101.69, well above the 95.28 he has averaged over the last 12 months, and won nine of the first 12 legs.
Schindler averaged 99.51 and hit six 180s, but converted only 28 per cent of his chances at a double. That was the difference: Van Veen was at 37.
Van Veen equals his best Grand Slam run, a quarter-final in 2024. He plays Nathan Aspinall on Saturday at 8:45pm, with at least £35,000 already secured.
